name: Glow in the Dark Stickers
seoTitle: Glow in the Dark Stickers, Custom Printed With Your Logo
seoDescription: Custom glow in the dark stickers on phosphorescent vinyl that charges in light and glows after dark. Logos, labels, safety marks and event stickers.
h1: Custom Glow in the Dark Stickers
tagline: Phosphorescent vinyl that soaks up light all day and glows pale green when the lights go off.
quickAnswer: Glow in the dark stickers are printed on vinyl with a phosphorescent layer that absorbs light and releases it as a soft green glow in darkness, for up to 8 hours after a full charge. They are used for logos, product labels, safety and exit marks, kids' rooms and event stickers, in any shape or size. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.
highlights: Finish: gloss or matte, laminate optional

sections.h2: The lights go off and the sticker keeps going
sections.html:
Glow film works like the hands on an old watch. A layer of strontium aluminate pigment under the print absorbs daylight or room light, then releases it slowly as a green glow once the room goes dark. Nothing is powered, nothing is wired, and the effect repeats every time the sticker is charged. That is the difference from its sibling, our custom reflective sticker range: reflective film only lights up when a headlight or flashlight hits it and is dead in a dark room, while glow film shines on its own but is useless on a road where no one is standing in the dark looking at it. Glow is for indoor spaces and events; reflective is for traffic.

Orders come from bars and venues, bands, escape rooms, kids' brands, candle and skincare makers wanting a label that surprises in the bathroom at night, and facilities managers marking stairs, switches and exits.

sections.h2: How long it glows and what charges it
sections.html:
The glow is brightest in the first 15 to 30 minutes and fades gradually; in a fully dark room it stays visible for up to 8 hours after a good charge. Brightness depends almost entirely on the charge, and the charge depends on the light.

  • Direct sunlight: 5 to 10 minutes gives a full charge. The best source by far.
  • Bright LED or fluorescent room light: 30 to 60 minutes for a full charge; a normal lit day in a shop or kitchen is plenty.
  • Warm, dim incandescent bulbs: slow and weak. A sticker in a dim hallway never charges well.
  • UV or black light: charges in seconds and makes the film glow intensely while the lamp is on, which is why glow stickers are popular at club and festival events.
  • Through a window: works, but window glass filters some UV, so expect a shorter glow than direct sun.

The film does not wear out from charging. After years of daily cycles it glows as it did on day one, as long as the surface is kept clean and out of harsh direct sun, which yellows the laminate over time.

sections.h2: Designing for a sticker that has two looks
sections.html:
Every glow sticker has a daytime look and a night look, and the two are not the same. The glow layer is a pale greenish white, and anything printed over it blocks the glow in proportion to how dark the ink is. Plan both views before you send the file.

sections.h2: Where glow stickers are useful, beyond the ceiling stars
sections.html: Glow in the dark labels do real jobs. Light switch and outlet markers help in a rental or a hotel room. Stair-edge and door-frame marks guide people out during a power cut. Labels on a nightstand product, a candle or a kids' bath bottle are found without turning the lights on. Venues use glow logo stickers on walls, pillars and cups so the brand is visible on a dark dance floor and under black light; bands hand them out knowing they end up on bedroom walls. Escape rooms hide clues on them. Camping and marine brands mark tent zips, cooler latches and boat steps. Related visibility materials are grouped under the feature-based sticker categories if a project needs glow on one item and reflective on another.

sections.h2: Outdoors, bathrooms and the laminate question
sections.html: Glow vinyl is a film, not paper, so steam and splashes in a bathroom do not bother it, and a matte or gloss laminate makes it safe for a dishwasher on a bottle or a cup. Laminate dims the glow very slightly and is worth it anywhere the sticker is handled or washed; skip it on a ceiling or a wall where nothing touches it. Outdoors the film holds up for a few years in the shade, but all-day direct sun will yellow it, so a glow label on a cooler or a boat is fine while a glow sticker on a south-facing sign is not. If the main need is a sticker that survives water and weather first, with glow as a bonus, start from our custom waterproof sticker range and ask for a glow version of the same design.

sections.h2: Ordering glow in the dark stickers with your logo
sections.html:
1. Decide what should glow: the whole shape, the background or the logo itself. Mark it on the artwork or tell us and free design support will set it up.
  2. Send the file as vector (AI, EPS, SVG, PDF) or a 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size. Light colors and bare-film areas should be clearly separated from dark areas.
  3. Choose the shape and size. Die cut to the outline, or circles, stars, arrows, rectangles, from 0.5" up to 24" x 36".
  4. Pick permanent adhesive for walls, products and safety marks, or removable for rentals, events and kids' rooms.
  5. Approve the free digital proof, which shows the daytime and glow views. Production takes 5 to 7 business days, with free FedEx shipping in the United States.

The minimum is 100 stickers and prices start at $0.30 per sticker depending on size and quantity; glow film costs more than plain vinyl, so many buyers print the bulk of a design on standard vinyl from the Die Cut Stickers home page and a smaller glow run as the premium version.

faqs.q: How long do custom glow in the dark stickers glow after the lights go out?
faqs.a: Up to 8 hours in a fully dark room after a good charge, brightest in the first 15 to 30 minutes and fading gradually. The glow is only as strong as the charge: ten minutes of direct sun or an hour of bright room light gives the full effect, a dim hallway gives much less.

faqs.q: What color do glow in the dark stickers glow?
faqs.a: Pale green. That is the color of strontium aluminate pigment, which glows longest and brightest of the safe phosphorescent pigments. Light tints printed over the film shift the glow slightly toward the tint, but dark inks block it, so a logo printed in black appears as a silhouette against a green glow.

faqs.q: Can my logo itself glow instead of the background?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the better design. We print the background in your brand colors and leave the logo or lettering as bare glow film, so the mark lights up in the dark. The reverse, a dark logo on a glowing background, also works but reads as a silhouette.

faqs.q: Do glow in the dark stickers work in daylight?
faqs.a: In daylight they look like an ordinary printed sticker with a pale cream background where the film is bare. The glow is invisible until the room is dark, so the sticker has to work as a normal design by day. We show both the daytime and the glow view on the proof.

faqs.q: Will glow stickers charge under normal indoor lighting?
faqs.a: Under bright LED or fluorescent light, yes, in 30 to 60 minutes. Dim warm bulbs charge them slowly and weakly. A sticker in a kitchen, shop or office that is lit all day will glow well at night; one in a dark corridor needs a spell of brighter light to perform.

faqs.q: Can glow in the dark labels go on a candle or a skincare bottle?
faqs.a: Yes. The film handles bathroom steam, and with a laminate it survives washing and handling. Keep the ingredient text in dark ink on a pale area so it reads by day, and leave a glow panel or the logo as bare film so the product is easy to find on a nightstand or shelf.

faqs.q: Are glow in the dark stickers safe for a child's bedroom?
faqs.a: Yes. The pigment is strontium aluminate, which is non-toxic and non-radioactive; it replaced the older zinc sulfide and radium types decades ago. For a bedroom choose removable adhesive so stars and shapes can be moved as the room changes without marking the paint.

faqs.q: Can I use glow in the dark stickers outside?
faqs.a: In shade or indirect light, for a few years. All-day direct sun yellows the film and dulls the glow, so a glow mark on a cooler, tent or boat step is fine while a glow sticker on a sunny sign is not. For outdoor visibility to traffic, reflective film is the right product.

faqs.q: Does the glow wear out after repeated charging?
faqs.a: No. The pigment charges and discharges indefinitely without losing strength; stickers charged daily for years glow as they did when new. What does age the sticker is harsh sunlight on the laminate and surface dirt, both of which filter the light going in and the glow coming out.

faqs.q: Can glow in the dark stickers be cut into stars, arrows and other shapes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unprinted glow film die cut into stars, arrows, numbers or your logo outline is the simplest glow sticker and glows evenly across the whole shape. Shapes run from 0.5" up to 24" x 36", and small shapes can be supplied on kiss cut sheets for easy peeling.

faqs.q: What is the smallest order of custom glow in the dark stickers?
faqs.a: 100 stickers per design. Prices start at $0.30 per sticker, set by size and quantity, with glow film priced above plain vinyl. Production is 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free proof, with free FedEx shipping in the United States.

faqs.q: Can glow stickers be used as exit and stair markers in a building?
faqs.a: Yes, for wayfinding marks on stair edges, door frames, handrails and switches that stay visible in a power cut. Charge them with the normal building lighting. For marks that have to meet a fire code, confirm the specification with your inspector, since some codes require a certified photoluminescent product.
